decision.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its target interest rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in March suggests that economic activity has continued to strengthen and that the labor market is beginning to improve.
changes.explanation: The Fed updated its view on the calendar from January to March and noted that the job market is starting to get better.

changes.quote: Growth in household spending has picked up recently but remains constrained by high unemployment, modest income growth, lower housing wealth, and tight credit.
changes.explanation: Consumer spending has accelerated slightly, but high joblessness and tight credit continue to hold it back.

changes.quote: Housing starts have edged up but remain at a depressed level.
changes.explanation: Home construction has shown slight improvement but stays at very low levels.

changes.quote: In light of improved functioning of financial markets, the Federal Reserve has closed all but one of the special liquidity facilities that it created to support markets during the crisis.
changes.explanation: Emergency lending programs created during the crisis have been mostly shut down because financial markets are working better.

tone_quotes.quote: Although the pace of economic recovery is likely to be moderate for a time, the Committee anticipates a gradual return to higher levels of resource utilization in a context of price stability.

The Committee will maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and continues to anticipate that economic conditions, including low rates of resource utilization, subdued inflation trends, and stable inflation expectations, are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate for an extended period.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.6% APR costs about $56.67 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.8% and moved +9 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.07% would rise by about $16.60 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 9.9%, and employers added an average of 19k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.3% over the past year (March 2010); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved 0 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.42% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed plans to keep rates exceptionally low for an extended period.
